name: fun-pet-code-cleaners
description: A MobaXterm-inspired screensaver: when you go idle, a pet crawls across your code and sweeps it clean — rendered directly in the editor with the native Decoration API.

commands.title: Pet Screensaver: Clear Downloaded Asset Cache

petScreensaver.cleanPetUrl.markdownDescription:
URL of an animated GIF of the pet sweeping/cleaning, ideally with a transparent background.

A local absolute file path also works. Leave empty to use the bundled default pet.

**Note:** VS Code cannot render a remote URL inside an editor decoration ([vscode#11055](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/11055)), so the image is downloaded once and cached on disk. Use an asset around `petSize` pixels tall for best results.

petScreensaver.idleTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds of inactivity before the screensaver activates. Typing, moving the cursor, or scrolling stops it instantly.

petScreensaver.enabled.description: Enable the idle screensaver. When off, the pet only appears via the 'Start Now' command.

enumDescriptions: Janitor with a spray bottle and cloth

petScreensaver.pets.markdownDescription: Which bundled pets can join the crew. Leave empty for all of them. The **Pet Screensaver: Choose Pets** command edits this for you.

petScreensaver.minPets.description: Fewest pets that can turn up at once.

petScreensaver.maxPets.description: Most pets that can turn up at once. Each run picks a random number in this range.

enumDescriptions: A door opens on a line and the pet steps out
A ladder leans against the code and the pet climbs up
The pet drops in on a rope, window-washer style
The pet scurries in from the side of the screen

petScreensaver.entrances.markdownDescription: How pets arrive. Each pet leaves the same way it came in.

petScreensaver.petSize.markdownDescription:
Pet height in pixels. Leave at `0` to match your editor's line height, which keeps pets small and cute.

Some builds of Chromium ignore sizing on decoration images — if a pet renders at its natural size, resize the source asset instead.

petScreensaver.speed.description: How fast pets sweep, in characters per second. Low values look unhurried and deliberate.

petScreensaver.travelSpeed.markdownDescription: How fast pets walk between lines, in lines per second. This is what makes a pet cross a gap in your code on foot rather than appearing to jump — lower it to make the walk more deliberate.

petScreensaver.exitAnimation.markdownDescription: When you come back, let pets run home and leave the way they arrived. The dimming clears instantly either way — only the pets linger, for about a second. Turn off to have everything vanish on the first keystroke.

petScreensaver.customPets.markdownDescription:
Your own pets. Each entry needs an `id` and a `sprites.clean` image; `walk`, `run`, `climb` and `hang` are optional and fall back to `clean`.

Values can be http(s) URLs or absolute local paths. Animated GIFs and animated SVGs both work.

```json
{
  "id": "my-pet",
  "label": "My Pet",
  "sprites": { "clean": "https://example.com/sweep.gif" },
  "entrances": ["edge"]
}
```

petScreensaver.wipeEffect.description: Fade out code as pets sweep over it. Purely visual — your file is never modified.

petScreensaver.wipeOpacity.description: How faint swept code becomes when the wipe effect is on. 0 is invisible, 1 is untouched.

petScreensaver.lineHeightOverride.description: Editor line height in pixels, used to size and centre pets. Leave at 0 to derive it automatically from your editor font settings.
